tests.label: Define group and period
tests.question: Define the terms group and period in the Periodic Table.
tests.studentAnswer: A group is a vertical column in the Periodic Table while a period is a horizontal row.

tests.label: Define group only
tests.question: Define the terms group and period in the Periodic Table.
tests.studentAnswer: A group is a vertical column.

tests.label: Swapped group/period
tests.question: Define the terms group and period in the Periodic Table.
tests.studentAnswer: A group is a horizontal row and a period is a vertical column.

tests.label: Group 1 properties full
tests.question: State two physical properties of Group 1 elements.
tests.studentAnswer: They are soft metals and have low densities.

tests.label: Group 1 one property
tests.question: State two physical properties of Group 1 elements.

tests.label: Group 1 wrong properties
tests.question: State two physical properties of Group 1 elements.

tests.label: Group 1 reactivity trend
tests.question: Describe the trend in reactivity of Group 1 elements down the group.

tests.label: Group 1 reactivity explain
tests.question: Explain why the reactivity of Group 1 elements increases down the group.
tests.studentAnswer: The atomic size increases down the group. The outermost electron is further from the nucleus and is more easily lost.

tests.label: Group 1 reactivity partial
tests.question: Explain why the reactivity of Group 1 elements increases down the group.
tests.studentAnswer: The outermost electron is more easily lost.

tests.label: Halogen reactivity trend
tests.question: State the trend in reactivity of halogens down Group 17.

tests.label: Halogen trend wrong
tests.question: State the trend in reactivity of halogens down Group 17.

tests.label: Halogen reactivity explain
tests.question: Explain why the reactivity of halogens decreases down Group 17.
tests.studentAnswer: Atomic size increases down the group. The attraction between the nucleus and incoming electron becomes weaker, making it harder to gain an electron.

tests.label: Halogen explain partial
tests.question: Explain why the reactivity of halogens decreases down Group 17.
tests.studentAnswer: It becomes harder to gain an electron.

tests.label: Noble gas unreactive
tests.question: Explain why noble gases are chemically unreactive.
tests.studentAnswer: Noble gases have a stable electron arrangement with a complete outermost shell.

tests.label: Noble gas partial
tests.question: Explain why noble gases are chemically unreactive.
tests.studentAnswer: They have a stable electron arrangement.

tests.label: Noble gas wrong
tests.question: Explain why noble gases are chemically unreactive.

tests.label: Rate vs temperature
tests.question: Explain why the rate of reaction increases when temperature increases. (3 marks)
tests.studentAnswer: Particles move faster and collide more often. More particles have enough energy to overcome activation energy.

tests.label: Rate vs surface area
tests.question: Explain why powdered calcium carbonate reacts faster than marble chips with hydrochloric acid. (3 marks)
tests.studentAnswer: Powdered calcium carbonate has a larger surface area. More particles are exposed to the acid, so there are more frequent collisions.

tests.label: Halogen displacement
tests.question: Explain why chlorine can displace bromine from a bromide solution.
tests.studentAnswer: Chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces bromine from its compound.

tests.question: Explain why chlorine can displace bromine from a bromide solution.
